what: does the FOLD-side bag10 member set share the ranking-side cache defect?  The desk, 2026-09-09: the ranking member cache keyed on seed+leaves only, so ranking members 6-10 were fitted on the GATED class (193,800) and mixed with the ungated 1-5.  If the fold side shares it, d-bag10-255-free.npz is re-emitted and this lane's v9 arm pin d32a993b moves.
the_test: a gated-class member cannot move the rows the gate removes, so the defect is a SUPPORT difference and shows as a systematic block: rows moved by every ungated member and by no gated one.  Fit churn moves single rows at the margin; a class difference moves a block.
head: experiments/exp-046-surfacefit/work/d-bundle-ungated1299-guard995.npz
members: d-bundle-placebo{1..10}-255-free.npz, the fold-side vectors on disk
read: NO -- the fold side does NOT share the defect.  ZERO rows on every fold are moved by all of members 1-5 and none of 6-10, or the reverse; the unions differ by 56 / 76 / 0 rows out of 88k / 102k / 70k, and january is identical to the row.  A gated-class member set would leave a block of thousands, not a margin of tens.  The fold-side member censuses agree exactly as well (kept/in_pool/out_pool identical for members 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 across bag-arm.json and bag-10.json).
what_this_does_not_prove: this tests SUPPORT -- which rows each member moves -- which is exactly the signature the gated/ungated class difference produces.  A defect that changed member VALUES without changing their support would not show here.  It is evidence on the specific defect described, not a general clearance of the member set.
